entries.subject: ESA/Hubble heic1310a
entries.finding: Hubble image of the Ring Nebula (Messier 57): He II 469, H-beta 487, [O III] 502, continuum 645, H-alpha 656, [N II] 658 and [S II] 673 nm; 3179 × 3179 px over 2.10 × 2.10 arcmin. The file's embedded sky tags, used as they are: 0.0396 arcsec per pixel, north 11.7° left of vertical, the frame's centre at 283.3967177°, 33.0289252°. Not measured against Gaia here.

entries.subject: The shape of the Ring Nebula
entries.finding: O'Dell et al. (2013, Sect. III.1 and III.3), with O'Dell, Sabbadin & Henney (2007) as restated there, give the shape from long-slit spectra: expansion of 0.65 km/s per arcsec; a Main Ring 44 by 30 arcsec on the sky whose velocity ellipse is 19 km/s in [N II] and [S II] and 9 km/s in [O III]; and polar Lobes through its centre at 36 km/s in [N II], 28 in [O III] and 20 in He II. Kastner et al. (2025, Sect. IV) find the same form in the CO cube: a thin ellipsoidal shell seen nearly pole-on, open at both poles, with an elongated body of radius 2.3e17 cm through the openings. The picture's light is laid on those walls. Two earlier attempts are not used: a Nebula Lab volume of the 2007 ellipsoid, whose 192 px slices lost the picture's detail, and an even fill of that ellipsoid around the flat picture, which guessed where the light lies and read as a flat picture from every direction but the Sun's.

entries.subject: Stars in the picture
entries.finding: The photograph first kept its stars, which stood on the nebula's plane whatever their own distances. The Nebula Lab's NOX removes them and keeps the nebula's structure. The glow of the brightest stars remains. A second pass over a quarter-size copy takes saturated stars, but on this picture it also took real nebula, so it is not used. The galaxies' glow fill, which needs a star table, erased nebula around the stars that light it and is not used on nebulae.
